comments.content: The `ssr` function caches only the root path (`/`). For SPA routes like `/albums`, `/photos`, etc., this will fetch and cache `/` instead of the actual route. Since the app is an SPA, serving the cached `/` (index.html) for all routes is correct behavior, but the cache key should be the actual request URL to avoid redundant network requests for each route. Consider caching `event.request` instead of `url` (which is always `/`).
The `appResources` function checks `APP_RESOURCES.includes(url.pathname)` again, but this is already guaranteed by the fetch event handler. The check is redundant and can be removed.

Using `cache.match(url.pathname)` with a string path instead of the full Request/URL may fail to match cached entries that were stored with `cache.put(event.request, ...)` (which uses the full URL as key). Use `cache.match(event.request)` or `cache.match(url)` for consistency.

The `cache.put(event.request, response.clone())` caches the response under the full request URL (including query params). However, the cache match at line 80 uses only `url.pathname` (no query params). This inconsistency can cause cache misses. Use `cache.match(event.request)` to match by the full request.
